cards.name: live_and_ancilla_shared_across_commuting_span
cards.identity: Let the Toffoli-level op list contain k >= 2 gates g_1 < g_2 < ... < g_k (positions p_1 < ... < p_k, not necessarily adjacent) of the form ccz(a,b,c_i) or ccx(a,b,c_i) that share the SAME unordered control pair {a,b} but may have different targets c_i. Replace the whole span [p_1, p_k] by: (1) at p_1, and_compute(a,b -> t) on a fresh CLEAN ancilla t [4 T]; (2) each g_i -> cz(t,c_i) (for ccz) or cx(t,c_i) (for ccx) [0 T]; (3) immediately after p_k, and_uncompute(t) = measure t in the X basis and apply a classically controlled cz(a,b) fix-up [0 T]; (4) every other op strictly inside the span is left EXACTLY where it is, untouched. Total 4 T for the group instead of 4k T (book rule) or 7k T (naive). Several groups may be live simultaneously or nested, each with its own ancilla; ancillas are released at their uncompute and may be reused by a later disjoint group.
cards.correctness: Gidney's temporary logical-AND: and_compute puts t in |a AND b> (up to the gadget's measured Clifford fix-ups) using 4 T, and and_uncompute restores t to |0> with 0 T by X-basis measurement plus a classically controlled cz(a,b), whose two measurement branches apply the same operator on the data up to a global phase, so the specification contract (function + ancilla return + per-branch phase consistency, sum|c_m|^2 = 1) holds. The data action is correct because ccz(a,b,c) = cz(t,c) and ccx(a,b,c) = cx(t,c) pointwise whenever t holds a AND b, and these controlled gates read t without writing it, so t stays |a AND b> throughout the span. The only new requirement versus the existing contiguous-run rule is that the value a AND b be unchanged over the span: this is guaranteed by the trigger's condition that no op inside the span WRITES a or b. Ops inside the span acting on the targets c_i, or on any other wire, are irrelevant: they commute with t (they do not touch it) and they are not moved, so the circuit's own ordering of target-side operations (including the h's that turn ccz into ccx and the x's on targets) is preserved verbatim. No gate is reordered, so no commutation obligation beyond the a,b read-only check is incurred.
cards.trigger: Build the write-set of each op (for h/x/z/s/sdg/t/tdg: its qubit; for cx: the target; for cz/ccz: nothing, they are diagonal and only read; for ccx: the target; for measure and classically controlled gates: their qubit(s)). Collect all ccz/ccx ops and group them by unordered control pair {a,b} (for ccz all three qubits are symmetric, so each ccz offers three candidate pairs; choose pairs greedily by descending group size, then by shortest span). A candidate group {p_1..p_k}, k >= 2, is legal iff no op at a position in (p_1, p_k) writes a or b, and neither a nor b is measured in the span. Emit one match per legal group, largest k first; after emitting a group, remove its members from the pool so each Toffoli is lowered once. A degenerate sub-case worth emitting first: two ccz on the IDENTICAL triple {a,b,c} with no op writing a, b or c between them cancel outright (ccz^2 = I, diagonal), removing 8 T with no ancilla.
cards.expected_effect: modred_21 is 17 ccz + 30 h + 24 x + 3 cx on 11 qubits, and the existing contiguous-run rule measured exactly 119 -> 68 = 4 x 17, i.e. it shared NOTHING here: every run had length 1 because the h's that re-express ccz as ccx on the target wire, and the x's on targets, sit between consecutive Toffolis and break contiguity (trigrams 'ccz h x' x14, 'h ccz h' x11, 'x h ccz' x10). None of those intervening ops writes a control, so dropping the contiguity requirement and keeping the AND ancilla live across the span should fuse most of the Toffolis of each modular-reduction stage, whose comparison/modulus control pair is held fixed while the target sweeps the register. Each fused member drops from 4 T to 0 T. Expect roughly 5 groups of average size 2-3 to fire, i.e. about 5 Toffolis staying at 4 T and about 5 more becoming free, at the cost of 1-3 extra clean ancillas (T-count is the first tie-break, so the qubit growth is accepted). Estimated 68 -> about 48 T, well under pyzx's 73 and BQSKit's 119.
cards.source: C. Gidney, 'Halving the cost of quantum addition', Quantum 2, 74 (2018) (temporary logical-AND: 4 T compute, 0 T measured uncompute); C. Jones, PRA 87, 022328 (2013) (4-T Toffoli); commutation/DAG-based regrouping as in Y. Nam, N. Ross, Y. Su, A. Childs, D. Maslov, 'Automated optimization of large quantum circuits with continuous parameters', npj QI 4, 23 (2018).

cards.name: x_frame_normalized_and_sharing_span
cards.identity: Pauli-X frame propagation through CCZ, used to make a control pair read-only so one AND ancilla serves a whole span. Core identities (exact, Clifford-only cost): X_a CCZ(a,b,c) = CCZ(a,b,c) CZ(b,c) X_a ; X_b CCZ(a,b,c) = CCZ(a,b,c) CZ(a,c) X_b ; X_a X_b CCZ(a,b,c) = CCZ(a,b,c) CZ(b,c) CZ(a,c) Z_c X_a X_b ; X_a CZ(a,b) = CZ(a,b) Z_b X_a. Procedure on a span [p_1,p_k] of CCZ gates g_i = ccz(a,b,c_i) sharing the unordered pair {a,b} (targets c_i arbitrary, gates need NOT be adjacent): sweep the span left to right carrying two frame bits (alpha on a, beta on b), both initially 0. (1) every `x` gate on a (resp. b) inside the span is DELETED and flips alpha (resp. beta); (2) at each g_i = ccz(a,b,c_i) emit ccz(a,b,c_i) followed by cz(b,c_i) if alpha, cz(a,c_i) if beta, z(c_i) if alpha AND beta - all Clifford, 0 T; (3) an intervening cz(a,q) emits cz(a,q) then z(q) if alpha (symmetrically for b); (4) at the end of the span emit x(a) if alpha, x(b) if beta, restoring the frame. Every op not touching a or b (the h's and x's on target wires, cx/h on unrelated wires) is left verbatim in place, in its original position - nothing is reordered. The span now writes neither a nor b, so lower it once: and_compute(a,b -> t) on a fresh CLEAN ancilla t immediately before p_1 [4 T]; each g_i -> cz(t,c_i) [0 T]; and_uncompute(t) immediately after p_k (X-basis measurement + classically controlled cz(a,b)) [0 T]. Total 4 T for the whole span instead of 4k T (book rule) or 7k T (naive). Degenerate sub-case emitted first and preferred: after frame normalization two CCZ on the IDENTICAL triple with no write to a, b or c between them are deleted outright (CCZ^2 = I, diagonal), -8 T and no ancilla. Spans are chosen greedily by descending k; the ancilla is released at its uncompute and reused by later disjoint spans.
cards.correctness: Each propagation identity is an exact conjugation of a diagonal gate by a Pauli: CCZ = diag(1,...,1,-1) flips sign on |111>, so X_a CCZ X_a is diagonal with the -1 on |011>, i.e. CZ(b,c) CCZ; similarly for X_b, and the two-flip case puts the -1 on |001> giving CCZ CZ(b,c) CZ(a,c) Z_c. Because every correction is Clifford and diagonal on the target wire, and because the X gates are moved only past gates that are diagonal on a and b (ccz, cz, z, s, t, and the X gates themselves), the sweep is a sequence of exact local rewrites: the product of the emitted ops equals the original span operator exactly, up to no phase at all, and the frame is closed at the span end so the circuit outside the span is untouched. After normalization no op in the span writes a or b, so the value a AND b is constant over the span; Gidney's temporary logical-AND puts t = |a AND b> with 4 T and returns it to |0> with 0 T by X-basis measurement plus a classically controlled cz(a,b), whose two measurement branches apply the same data operator up to global phase, so the relaxed contract (function, ancilla returns to |0>, per-branch phase consistency with sum|c_m|^2 = 1) holds. CCZ(a,b,c) = CZ(t,c) pointwise whenever t holds a AND b, and CZ(t,c) only reads t, so t is undisturbed through the span. No gate is reordered except the deleted/re-emitted X gates on a and b, whose movement is justified by the identities above.
cards.trigger: Toffoli-level circuits only (return [] otherwise). Write-set: h/x/s/sdg/t/tdg -> its qubit (x is a WRITE but a recoverable one, see below); cx/ccx -> target only; z/cz/ccz -> nothing (diagonal, read-only); measure and classically controlled gates -> all their qubits. Collect the ccz/ccx ops (for ccx(a,b,c) the pair must be {a,b}; for ccz all three qubits are symmetric, so each ccz offers three candidate pairs) and group them by unordered pair {a,b}. A candidate span [p_1,p_k], k >= 2, is LEGAL iff every op strictly inside the span that touches a or b is one of: `x` on a or b; `z`, `cz`, `ccz` (diagonal, read-only); another member of the group. Any `h` on a or b, any `cx`/`ccx` writing a or b, any s/sdg/t/tdg on a or b, or any measurement of a or b, makes the span illegal - shrink the span to the longest legal prefix/suffix with k >= 2 rather than discarding the pair. Ops touching neither a nor b impose no condition whatsoever. Enumerate candidate pairs by descending group size then shortest span; after emitting a span remove its members from the pool so each Toffoli is lowered once. Emit identical-triple cancellations first. Require k >= 2 (k = 1 gives no gain over the book rule).
cards.expected_effect: modred_21 is 17 ccz + 30 h + 24 x + 3 cx on 11 qubits and the existing contiguous-run AND rule measured exactly 119 -> 68 = 4 x 17, i.e. it shared nothing: every run had length 1. The blocker is the `x` gates, not the `h` gates - the h's sit on TARGET wires (they are the ccz<->ccx conjugations, trigrams 'h ccz h' x14/x11 and the QASM note `gate ccz = h ccx h`), while modular reduction toggles its comparison/modulus CONTROLS with `x` to get control-on-zero (trigrams 'ccz h x' x14, 'x h ccz' x10, 'h x x' x8, 'x x h' x7). A read-only-control test therefore fails on every pair, which is exactly why the previous span rule never fired. Absorbing those x's into a propagated X frame removes the only obstruction: each reduction stage holds one control pair fixed (modulo X toggles) while the target sweeps the register, so the 17 ccz should fall into roughly 4-6 pairs-with-multiplicity. Each span costs 4 T no matter its length, so about 5 spans covering ~14 ccz give 5 x 4 = 20 T plus ~3 leftover singletons at 4 T = 12 T, i.e. 68 -> about 32-48 T, at the cost of 1-2 extra clean ancillas (T-count is the first tie-break, qubit growth is accepted). Well under pyzx's 73 and BQSKit's 119. All corrections (cz, z, x) and all AND uncomputes are free.
cards.source: C. Gidney, 'Halving the cost of quantum addition', Quantum 2, 74 (2018) (temporary logical-AND: 4 T compute, 0 T measured uncompute); C. Jones, PRA 87, 022328 (2013) (4-T Toffoli); Pauli-frame / X-propagation through diagonal multi-controlled gates as in M. Amy, D. Maslov, M. Mosca, 'Polynomial-time T-depth optimization of Clifford+T circuits' (IEEE TCAD 2014) and Y. Nam, N. Ross, Y. Su, A. Childs, D. Maslov, 'Automated optimization of large quantum circuits with continuous parameters', npj QI 4, 23 (2018) (Pauli/Hadamard gadgetization and commutation-based regrouping).

cards.name: and_ancilla_value_tracking_span
cards.identity: Keep ONE temporary logical-AND ancilla live across a span of CCZ/CCX gates that share a control pair, and repair the ancilla with free Clifford gates whenever the circuit's own X gates change the controls' values - instead of moving the X gates or propagating an X frame through the CCZ gates. Let the op list contain gates g_1 < ... < g_k (positions p_1 < ... < p_k, k >= 2, not necessarily adjacent) of the form ccz(a,b,c_i) or ccx(a,b,c_i) on the same unordered pair {a,b}. Rewrite ONLY these three things, leaving every other op byte-for-byte in its original position and order: (1) immediately before p_1 insert and_compute(a,b -> t) on a fresh CLEAN ancilla t [4 T], establishing t = a AND b; (2) replace each g_i by cz(t,c_i) (for ccz) or cx(t,c_i) (for ccx) [0 T]; (3) immediately AFTER each op `x(a)` lying strictly inside the span, insert cx(b,t), and after each `x(b)` insert cx(a,t) [0 T, Clifford]; (4) immediately after p_k insert and_uncompute(t) = X-basis measurement of t plus a classically controlled cz(a,b) [0 T], releasing t for reuse by a later disjoint span. The whole span costs 4 T regardless of k, versus 4k T (current book rule) or 7k T (naive).
cards.correctness: Invariant: at every point of the span, t holds the current computational-basis value of a AND b. It holds after and_compute (Gidney/Jones temporary AND, 4 T). The only ops in the span permitted to change the value of a or b are `x` gates on a or b (the trigger forbids h, s/sdg, t/tdg, cx/ccx writing a or b, and measurement of a or b; z/cz/ccz are diagonal and change no basis value). After x(a), write a' = a XOR 1; t stores the stale product a*b = (a' XOR 1)*b = b XOR a'*b, so applying cx(b,t) sets t = a'*b, restoring the invariant; symmetrically cx(a,t) after x(b). Repair gates use only b (resp. a), which is unchanged by that x, so the update is exact. Since t = a AND b is a deterministic function of the two control wires, the state never leaves (data basis state) tensor |a AND b>, and all intervening diagonal gates on a, b apply exactly the same phases as in the original circuit. Data action: CCZ(a,b,c) = CZ(t,c) and CCX(a,b,c) = CX(t,c) pointwise whenever t = a AND b, and these gates only READ t, so the invariant survives them. Nothing is reordered, so no commutation obligation beyond the value-tracking above. Finally and_uncompute returns t to |0> with 0 T; its two measurement branches apply the same data operator up to global phase, so the relaxed contract (function computed, ancilla returns to |0>, per-branch phase consistency, sum |c_m|^2 = 1) holds.
cards.trigger: Toffoli-level IRCircuit only (return [] otherwise). Classify per op: VALUE-PRESERVING on a wire = z, cz, ccz (diagonal, read-only) and, for cx/ccx, the control wires; RECOVERABLE WRITE = `x` on a single wire; HARD WRITE = h, s, sdg, t, tdg on the wire, the target of cx/ccx, measurement, or any classically controlled op on the wire. Collect all ccz/ccx ops; for ccx(a,b,c) the only candidate pair is the control pair {a,b}, for ccz all three qubits are symmetric so each ccz offers its three pairs. Group gates by unordered pair {a,b}. A span [p_1,p_k] over a group is LEGAL iff no op strictly inside it is a HARD WRITE to a or to b (ops touching neither wire impose no condition at all; `x` on a or b is allowed and triggers a repair insertion; `x` on target wires and the ccz<->ccx conjugating h's on target wires are irrelevant). If the maximal span is illegal, shrink to the longest legal contiguous sub-run of group members with k >= 2 rather than discarding the pair. Enumerate candidate pairs by descending k, then by shortest span; after emitting a span remove its member gates from the pool so each Toffoli is lowered exactly once. Require k >= 2 (k = 1 is already handled at 4 T by the book rule). Cap: at most one match per pair-and-span, so the match list is O(#ccz) and each apply() touches only its own span - no global re-synthesis, no search.

cards.name: and_ancilla_value_tracking_span
cards.identity: Keep ONE temporary logical-AND ancilla live across a span of CCZ/CCX gates that share a control pair, and repair the ancilla with free Clifford gates whenever the circuit's own X gates change the controls' values - instead of moving the X gates or propagating an X frame through the CCZ gates. Let the op list contain gates g_1 < ... < g_k (positions p_1 < ... < p_k, k >= 2, not necessarily adjacent) of the form ccz(a,b,c_i) or ccx(a,b,c_i) on the same unordered pair {a,b}. Rewrite ONLY these three things, leaving every other op byte-for-byte in its original position and order: (1) immediately before p_1 insert and_compute(a,b -> t) on a fresh CLEAN ancilla t [4 T], establishing t = a AND b; (2) replace each g_i by cz(t,c_i) (for ccz) or cx(t,c_i) (for ccx) [0 T]; (3) immediately AFTER each op `x(a)` lying strictly inside the span, insert cx(b,t), and after each `x(b)` insert cx(a,t) [0 T, Clifford]; (4) immediately after p_k insert and_uncompute(t) = X-basis measurement of t plus a classically controlled cz(a,b) [0 T], releasing t for reuse by a later disjoint span. The whole span costs 4 T regardless of k, versus 4k T (current book rule) or 7k T (naive).
cards.correctness: Invariant: at every point of the span, t holds the current computational-basis value of a AND b. It holds after and_compute (Gidney/Jones temporary AND, 4 T). The only ops in the span permitted to change the value of a or b are `x` gates on a or b (the trigger forbids h, s/sdg, t/tdg, cx/ccx writing a or b, and measurement of a or b; z/cz/ccz are diagonal and change no basis value). After x(a), write a' = a XOR 1; t stores the stale product a*b = (a' XOR 1)*b = b XOR a'*b, so applying cx(b,t) sets t = a'*b, restoring the invariant; symmetrically cx(a,t) after x(b). Repair gates use only b (resp. a), which is unchanged by that x, so the update is exact. Since t = a AND b is a deterministic function of the two control wires, the state never leaves (data basis state) tensor |a AND b>, and all intervening diagonal gates on a, b apply exactly the same phases as in the original circuit. Data action: CCZ(a,b,c) = CZ(t,c) and CCX(a,b,c) = CX(t,c) pointwise whenever t = a AND b, and these gates only READ t, so the invariant survives them. Nothing is reordered, so no commutation obligation beyond the value-tracking above. Finally and_uncompute returns t to |0> with 0 T; its two measurement branches apply the same data operator up to global phase, so the relaxed contract (function computed, ancilla returns to |0>, per-branch phase consistency, sum |c_m|^2 = 1) holds.

cards.name: complementary_control_toffoli_pair_collapse
cards.identity: Non-local collapse of a PAIR of Toffoli-level gates on the SAME qubit triple separated only by X gates on those wires. Step 0 (normalization, exact): wherever the op list contains h(w), ccz(u,v,w), h(w) with no other op on wire w between them, fuse to ccx(u,v,w); unmatched ccz stay ccz. Step 1: find two normalized Toffolis g_p, g_q (p<q) of the same type and on the same unordered triple {a,b,c} (for ccx also the same target c) such that EVERY op strictly between p and q either touches none of a,b,c, or is an `x` on one of a,b,c. Let alpha, beta, gamma be the parities of the numbers of x(a), x(b), x(c) gates strictly between. Step 2 (rewrite): delete BOTH Toffolis, leave every other op (including all those x gates) byte-for-byte where it is, and insert at position q the Clifford residue below, written in the wire VALUES at position q (A,B,C). CCZ case: the composite phase is (-1)^f with f = (A^alpha)(B^beta)(C^gamma) XOR A*B*C; the cubic terms cancel identically, so f expands over GF(2) into monomials of degree <= 2: emit z(q_i) for each surviving linear monomial, cz(q_i,q_j) for each surviving quadratic monomial, and ignore the constant (global phase). Explicitly: (alpha,beta,gamma)=(0,0,0) -> nothing (the two CCZ annihilate); (1,0,0) -> cz(b,c); (0,1,0) -> cz(a,c); (0,0,1) -> cz(a,b); (1,1,0) -> cz(a,c) cz(b,c) z(c); (1,0,1) -> cz(a,b) cz(b,c) z(b); (0,1,1) -> cz(a,b) cz(a,c) z(a); (1,1,1) -> cz(a,b) cz(a,c) cz(b,c) z(a) z(b) z(c). CCX case (target c): the composite flips c by (A^alpha)(B^beta) XOR A*B = alpha*B XOR beta*A XOR alpha*beta, so emit cx(b,c) if alpha, cx(a,c) if beta, x(c) if alpha AND beta (gamma is irrelevant: X on the target commutes with CCX); (alpha,beta)=(0,0) -> nothing. Cost: 8 T -> 0 T per matched pair, no ancilla, no measurement, nothing reordered. If the pair survives but its Toffolis were produced by the h-ccz-h fusion, re-emit the untouched h's only where the Toffoli was NOT deleted.
cards.correctness: CCZ = diag(1,...,1,-1) applies phase (-1)^{abc}; CCX flips c by a*b. X gates are the only ops between the two gates that touch a, b or c, so the values seen by g_p are exactly (A^alpha, B^beta, C^gamma) where A,B,C are the values at position q, and no op between reads or writes a, b, c otherwise (ops on disjoint wires commute with both Toffolis as tensor factors, so deleting the pair and inserting the residue at q is an identity on the full operator, not a reordering of anything else). Hence the composite of the two deleted CCZ is the diagonal operator (-1)^{(A^alpha)(B^beta)(C^gamma) + ABC}. Expanding over GF(2): (A^alpha)(B^beta)(C^gamma) = ABC + gamma*AB + beta*AC + alpha*BC + beta*gamma*A + alpha*gamma*B + alpha*beta*C + alpha*beta*gamma, so the ABC term cancels and the exponent is a degree-<=2 polynomial, i.e. a product of CZ and Z gates (plus a global phase) - Clifford, 0 T. The listed eight cases are this expansion. For CCX, X on the target commutes with CCX (CCX X_c = X_c CCX) so gamma only moves the x gates past, and the composite flip of c is (A^alpha)(B^beta) + AB = alpha*B + beta*A + alpha*beta, realized by cx(b,c), cx(a,c), x(c). Both rewrites are exact up to global phase, use no ancilla and no measurement, so the exact D[omega] check on the changed window decides them. Step 0 is the defining identity CCX(u,v,w) = H_w CCZ(u,v,w) H_w, applied only when the two h's are adjacent on wire w.
cards.trigger: Toffoli-level IRCircuit only (return [] otherwise; this never applies to Clifford+Rz angle circuits). (a) Normalize: scan for h(w) ... ccz(u,v,w) ... h(w) where the two h are the ops immediately preceding/following that ccz ON WIRE w (arbitrary ops on other wires may sit in between in the flat list) and record the fused ccx(u,v,w). (b) Index the normalized Toffolis by their qubit triple (unordered for ccz; (controls, target) for ccx). (c) For every pair p<q with the same key, scan the ops strictly between: ACCEPT the pair iff every such op has an empty intersection with {a,b,c} OR is exactly `x` on a, b or c; REJECT it the moment any other op touches a, b or c (h, s/sdg/t/tdg, z/cz on them, cx/ccx/ccz with any of a,b,c among its qubits, measurement, classically controlled op). Note that ANY op on other wires - including the 30 h's of this circuit when they sit on wires outside the triple - imposes no condition at all, which is what makes this non-local. (d) Accumulate alpha, beta, gamma from the x's seen. (e) Emit matches in order of increasing span (q-p), greedily removing both members from the pool so each Toffoli is consumed at most once; emit the (0,0,0) outright-cancellation matches first. Match count is O(#ccz^2) = O(300), each apply() edits only two positions plus <= 6 inserted Clifford gates - no search, no re-synthesis.
cards.expected_effect: modred_21 is 17 ccz + 30 h + 24 x + 3 cx on 11 qubits, 68 T under the book's per-Toffoli AND lowering (4 x 17: the AND rule shared nothing, so every Toffoli is an isolated 4 T). Modular reduction by a constant is compare-then-conditionally-correct: the same control/target triple is visited twice, once in the comparison and once in the correction or uncomputation, and the 24 x gates are exactly the control-on-zero / constant-modulus toggles that sit between those two visits (trigrams 'ccz h x' x14, 'x h ccz' x10, 'h x x' x8, 'x x h' x7, 'x ccz h' x2). Previous attempts failed because they required two Toffolis to share a CONTROL PAIR with stable values; here the requirement is the opposite and much weaker - the SAME triple, with X toggles explicitly allowed and absorbed into the residue - and the h's are no obstruction because they live on wires outside the triple or are fused away by step 0 ('h ccz h' x11). Each matched pair removes two Toffolis at 4 T each for free Cliffords: 2 pairs = 68 -> 52, 4 pairs = 68 -> 36. I expect 2-4 pairs among the 17 ccz (compare/correct mirror structure), i.e. 68 -> 36-52 T, versus pyzx 73, TKET 107, BQSKit 119. The rule also composes with the book: unmatched Toffolis keep their 4 T AND lowering, and qubit count is unchanged (no ancilla), so there is no tie-break cost.
